2 · Paste the post copy

One subsection. That is the only place the Senate's energy bill names Alaska.

Section 224(d) lets the Energy Secretary identify an Alaska congestion area only "subject to the approval of the Regulatory Commission of Alaska." Elsewhere there is no state approval step, only comments.

The Senate passed it 62 to 33 on November 19th. Murkowski and Sullivan voted yea.

Section 229 bars charging other customers any part of a data center's incremental cost. The data center keeps paying if it quits early. A State may bill data centers as their own class on less favorable terms.

The clause in its own words opens the carousel, four Senate roll calls follow, and the data center cost rule closes it.

The bill now heads to the House.
Does the RCA's approval step come back intact?

#AlaskaEnergy #FederalPowerAct #DataCenterPolicy

Editor's note

Shipped below the art floor at the five-round cap: total 8.17 against the 7.7 threshold, artwork craft 6.5. Slides 08 (blurred lower band) and 09 (soft pillow terrain, QA ground-edge warn) are the weakest frames. Slide 08's list markers are drawn 30x3 px rules, not dash characters, but at a glance they read like dash bullets; consider squares or numerals next time. Section 224(d) is an approval step, not a veto; replies should not say veto. Section 229 is not claimed to bind Alaska's utilities. 'Names Alaska once' means one subsection (five lines, all in 224(d), per a full-text grep). The routine ran at effort medium although settings carry high.
Section 224(d) gives the Regulatory Commission of Alaska an approval step over an Alaska congestion finding, not a veto, and the deck and caption word it as approval throughout. Whether section 229 reaches Alaska's intrastate utilities isn't settled by the text (229(e) says it expands and diminishes no one's jurisdiction), so slides 06 to 08 say what the section lets a State do and never that it binds Alaska's utilities. The claim that the RCA regulates Railbelt rates was killed for want of a fetched source, so the RCA's role rests on the bill's own words only, and nothing is claimed about the House beyond NPR's November 20th report that the bill "now heads to the House." The carved clause on 02 is canvas art, and the same words are printed verbatim in that slide's body, so the PDF text layer and screen readers carry it. The routine ran at effort medium, not the high the settings file carries.

  • Watch for any public response from the Regulatory Commission of Alaska to section 224(d). None was fetched this run, so don't describe the RCA's view in replies. After 48 hours note saves, comments and reposts for the instincts ledger.
